title: Hosted Canary Rollouts (GA) — Launch Brief (Draft)
content:
WORKING DRAFT — Hosted Canary Rollouts (GA) Launch Brief
Owner: Soojin Lee (Launch messaging)
Product lead: Marissa Cole
PM (policies/telemetry): Paula Mendes
Program manager: Talia Benson
Eng lead (Console): Dylan Brooks
SRE lead: Sean Gallagher
Security lead: Marcus Lin

Last updated: 2024-11-18
Target launch window: late Nov / early Dec (pending go/no-go)

---

1) What we’re launching (summary)
Hosted Canary Rollouts (GA) is a first-class workflow in the Redwood Console (and underlying control-plane/routing primitives) that lets customers safely roll out model/version changes on Hosted routes using percentage-based traffic splitting.

Customers can:
- Define baseline vs candidate model/version for a Hosted route
- Split traffic by percentage (manual steps; optional time-based progression where allowed)
- Configure guardrails (latency, error rate, token cost deltas; optional quality gates)
- Preview effective routing before applying changes
- Pause/rollback quickly
- View activity/audit history with actor attribution
- Monitor baseline vs candidate performance with per-variant metrics

What GA means here:
- Default-safe UX + validation to prevent high-risk configurations
- Deterministic policy evaluation and consistent data-plane behavior across regions
- Documented semantics for stickiness and streaming sessions/retries
- Audit log events for rollout lifecycle actions
- SLOs/alerts/runbooks for operational readiness

---

2) Target customers / ideal use cases
Primary (immediate adoption targets)
- Hosted customers operating production LLM features who currently:
  - “flip” model versions manually (high risk)
  - run shadow tests without traffic splitting
  - rely on bespoke routing logic in their app layer
- Teams doing frequent model iteration (prompt/model changes weekly) who need a safe and repeatable release process.

Customer profiles we should explicitly message to:
- AI-native SaaS teams with high QPS routes and tight latency budgets
- Mid-market + enterprise product teams that require:
  - auditability of config changes
  - clear rollback controls
  - reliable rollout semantics during incidents

Most compelling workloads:
- Customer support agents and copilots (quality regressions are costly)
- Search/rerank or summarization endpoints tied to user experience metrics
- Multi-region Hosted deployments needing consistent behavior

Non-target / not emphasized for GA launch messaging
- Self-managed (Private) customers (this is Hosted-only GA in this release)
- Advanced multi-variant experimentation (A/B/n beyond baseline + candidate is out of scope for GA)

---

3) Positioning & messaging (external + internal)
Messaging pillars
1) Safer releases for model changes
- “Roll out new model versions with controlled exposure and fast rollback.”

2) Built for production reality (latency/cost/reliability)
- “Guardrails ensure you don’t trade quality for cost—or cost for latency—without noticing.”

3) Operable and auditable
- “See exactly what changed, who changed it, and how the canary is performing.”

Suggested headline options (docs + release notes)
- “Percentage-based canary rollouts for Hosted routes—now GA.”
- “Safely roll out new model versions with guardrails, monitoring, and instant rollback.”

Key differentiators to highlight (vs ‘just a traffic split’)
- Guardrails integrated into the rollout workflow (error/latency/cost; optional quality gates)
- Preview “effective routing” before applying changes (reduces misconfig)
- Streaming semantics that prevent cross-variant mixing within a session
- Audit trail + export-ready events

Plain-language description for customers
“Create a rollout on any Hosted route, set the percent of traffic to your candidate model, monitor baseline vs candidate performance, and pause/rollback if metrics degrade.”

Limitations to be transparent about at GA
- Scope: Hosted routes only
- Variants: baseline + candidate (no multi-arm experiments in this GA)
- Stickiness is optional (trade-offs documented). Where disabled, traffic is weighted randomly per request.
- Quality gates are optional and may require additional setup (eval sets / monitoring integration).

---

4) Packaging, availability, and entitlements (draft)
Proposed availability
- GA enabled for: Dedicated Hosted plans + Enterprise Hosted plans by default
- Self-serve / Growth: available behind plan gating (TBD), or limited to “manual steps only” without timed progression (TBD)

Admin / RBAC notes
- New permissions:
  - rollouts:create
  - rollouts:edit
  - rollouts:pause
  - rollouts:rollback
  - rollouts:view_audit
- Default roles:
  - Org Admin: full access
  - Developer: create/edit/view, but pause/rollback may be restricted (TBD)

Open decision (needs alignment):
- Should “pause/rollback” be restricted to admins by default for enterprise, or allowed for on-call role?

---

5) Launch plan (phasing)
Phase A — Internal dogfood (target: complete)
- Feature flag enabled in staging + internal Hosted routes
- Console + control-plane + routing integration tested end-to-end

Phase B — Limited beta expansion (target: near-complete)
- Enable for select Hosted customers with high willingness to provide feedback
- Daily check-in on telemetry correctness, propagation staleness, and UX misconfig patterns

Phase C — GA
- Enable by default for eligible plans
- Publish docs + release notes
- Support enablement and on-call runbooks live

---

6) GA readiness checklist (go/no-go inputs)
Product / UX
- [ ] Console: create rollout wizard, percent step editor, guardrails config shipped
- [ ] Effective routing preview is accurate and explains layered policy resolution clearly
- [ ] Error states: RBAC/entitlement errors are actionable in UI
- [ ] Activity timeline + audit history UI (including empty/error states)
- [ ] Migration: Existing beta rollouts display correctly and can be edited without schema breakage

Control plane / policy
- [ ] Canonical rollout policy schema v2 is default (backward-compatible reads)
- [ ] Validation: percent sums, safe defaults, and misconfig prevention (e.g., 100% candidate without explicit confirmation / lacking guardrails per entitlement policy)
- [ ] Deterministic evaluation under load (no flapping variant selection)
- [ ] Propagation: monotonic versioning / race handling verified

Routing / data plane (Hosted)
- [ ] Weighted split routing behaves as expected across regions
- [ ] Stickiness semantics documented and tested (request-hash key behavior)
- [ ] Streaming: variant pinned at request start; retries reuse selection; no cross-variant mixing in a session
- [ ] Rollback/pause semantics: immediate effect for new requests; well-defined behavior for in-flight streams

Telemetry / monitoring
- [ ] Per-variant metrics (baseline vs candidate) available in dashboards:
  - error rate (4xx/5xx), p50/p95/p99 latency
  - token usage + token cost (where applicable)
  - throughput, timeouts
- [ ] Metric cardinality controls in place (route/variant/model version dims bounded)
- [ ] Canary comparison view usable (baseline vs candidate deltas)
- [ ] Alerts wired to on-call (error rate delta, latency delta, propagation staleness)

SRE / operations
- [ ] SLOs defined and published for:
  - policy evaluation latency
  - policy propagation staleness
  - availability of rollout endpoints
- [ ] Runbook: pause + rollback procedures tested by on-call
- [ ] “Known failure modes” documented (e.g., partial regional propagation, telemetry lag)

Security / compliance
- [ ] Audit events emitted for create/update/pause/rollback
- [ ] Payload review: no PII leakage; before/after diffs are bounded and readable
- [ ] Retention + export path documented (SIEM compatibility for enterprise)

Docs & support
- [ ] Docs: Hosted rollouts GA docs published (how-to + semantics + guardrails + troubleshooting)
- [ ] Support macros/FAQ updated (common questions and escalation path)
- [ ] Release notes finalized with limitations and best practices

---

7) Open risks & mitigations (current)
R1: Deterministic policy evaluation under high QPS
- Risk: inconsistent variant selection / perceived “wrong split”
- Mitigation: deterministic weighting logic; monotonic version propagation; load testing; “effective routing” preview aligns with runtime behavior
- Owner: Jordan Lee / Ethan Park

R2: Metric cardinality explosion (route x variant x model version)
- Risk: telemetry cost and dropped series; dashboards become unreliable
- Mitigation: enforce standards; sampling where needed; aggregation safeguards; limit dimensions
- Owner: Logan Wright / Thomas Baird

R3: Streaming rollback semantics confusing in incident
- Risk: in-flight streams continue on candidate after rollback; customers interpret as rollback “not working”
- Mitigation: document semantics; UI warning copy; runbook verification steps; consider “drain mode” messaging for long streams
- Owner: Emily Zhao / Sean Gallagher

R4: Misconfiguration leading to elevated 5xx (e.g., candidate not provisioned)
- Risk: customer causes outage via rollout settings
- Mitigation: validation (candidate availability), safe defaults, guardrail nudges; confirmation for risky actions; RBAC restrictions
- Owner: Jada Williams / Zachary Hill

R5: Policy propagation staleness during regional partial outage
- Risk: splits differ by region; customer sees inconsistent behavior
- Mitigation: staleness SLO/alerting; fallback behaviors documented; runbook + status communication
- Owner: Allison Grant / Ethan Park

R6: Audit log payload size / sensitivity
- Risk: audit export contains too much detail or sensitive prompt/config context
- Mitigation: payload bounding; explicit allowlist of fields; security review sign-off
- Owner: Kevin Osei / Marcus Lin

---

8) Internal comms plan (draft)
Channels
- #eng-releases: release train coordination, flag flip schedule, rollback criteria
- #support: enablement + FAQs + escalation points
- #product: launch messaging review + plan/entitlement updates
- Incident channel: if launch issues occur, use standard SEV triage process

Comms timeline (relative)
T-7 days
- Share final GA checklist status + open risks to stakeholders
- Dry run: pause/rollback in staging with SRE + Support present

T-2 days
- Confirm entitlements / gating
- Confirm docs and release notes are ready for publish

T-0 (Launch day)
- Announce internally with:
  - what’s enabled
  - who it’s for (plans)
  - known limitations
  - links to dashboards + runbook

T+1 day
- Post initial adoption + health snapshot (first 24h)

T+1 week
- Retro: what went well, issues, improvements, next iteration (A/B experimentation roadmap tie-in)

---

9) Go/No-Go decision & required approvers
Go/No-Go meeting owner: Talia Benson
Decision deadline: 24 hours before planned enablement

Required sign-offs (must be explicit)
- Product: Marissa Cole
- Engineering (Console): Dylan Brooks
- Platform/control plane: Priya Natarajan (or delegate Ethan Park)
- Routing: Mina Haddad
- Observability/SLOs: Sean Gallagher (with Allison Grant confirmation)
- Security/audit logs: Marcus Lin (with Kevin Osei confirmation)
- Docs readiness: Elliot Price (with Wei Chen confirmation)
- Release engineering: Connor O’Brien
- Support readiness: Dev Patel

Go criteria (minimum)
- No P0/P1 open bugs affecting routing correctness, rollback/pause, or schema migration
- SLO alerts configured and verified for staleness + error/latency deltas
- Audit events verified end-to-end in at least one enterprise-like environment
- Docs published (or scheduled) and support macros ready

No-Go triggers
- Any evidence of non-deterministic routing or incorrect weight application under load
- Propagation staleness above SLO without mitigation plan
- Telemetry missing or unusable for baseline vs candidate comparison
- Audit log payload flagged by Security review
